title: Paper architecture
topic: What can one folded sheet build?

cards.title: Stairs and arches cut from one card
cards.text: Two white cards, each cut and folded once: a stair climbing to a point, and a tunnel of arches. Nothing is added or glued, so each small building is still one sheet.

cards.title: Diamond platforms in a folded card
cards.text: The same move with fewer cuts. Slits across the fold lift a stack of diamond-shaped floors when the card opens to a right angle.

cards.title: Stepped pyramid with a copper back
cards.text: Parallel cuts turn every strip into a step. The copper underside shows through the gaps, so you can read which parts were pushed forward.

cards.title: Stage set with an arcaded courtyard
cards.text: A stage designer’s drawing of arches seen through arches. The paper tunnel does in real depth what this drawing does with perspective.

cards.title: Sheet cut in arcs and twisted upward
cards.text: Curved cuts in place of straight ones. The middle is lifted and turned, and the ribs left between the cuts lean into a small tower.

cards.title: Tower of strips with a twist inside
cards.text: A folded sheet cut into dozens of level strips. Some are pushed inward, and together they draw a twisting column down the middle.

cards.title: Cobweb Valentine
cards.text: Tissue cut in rings round its centre. Lift the thread and the rings rise into a cage over the portrait: the cut of the twisted sheet, in a valentine of 1830–40.

cards.title: Leaflet with boxes folded out of it
cards.text: A printed leaflet stood on end. Cuts across its folds push out three boxes, so a brochure with photographs of brick buildings becomes a small building itself.

cards.title: Pleated relief folded from one sheet
cards.text: No cuts here, only creases: fans of pleats that meet along zigzag ridges. The sheet keeps this shape with nothing added to it.

cards.title: Miura fold crease pattern
cards.text: The plan of a fold named for Koryo Miura and used in maps and solar panels. Two kinds of line mark the two directions of fold, in rows of slanted panels.

cards.title: Miura-ori sheets, folded
cards.text: The pattern in paper. Three sheets folded on the same zigzag rows, each taking a different surface: flat, arched and curled.

cards.title: Geometry of Miura-folded metamaterials
cards.text: Shows that a Miura-folded sheet behaves as it does because of the fold geometry alone, at any size: stretch it one way and it widens the other way too.
cards.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
cards.from: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

cards.title: Flat nets and what they fold into
cards.text: Four lettered pairs: a cross becomes a cube, a pinwheel of triangles becomes a ball, a scored sheet becomes a field of small peaks. The plan first, then the form.

cards.title: Three squares with curved creases
cards.text: Each white square has a few curved folds and no straight ones. The paper swells into shells and hollows, and below the squares join into one strip.

cards.title: Two discs of curved pleats
cards.text: Curved pleats run from the rim of each disc to its centre, overlapping like blades. One curved fold, repeated, turns a flat circle into a relief.

cards.title: A curved fold bends both sides
cards.text: Fold along a straight line and the two sides stay flat. Fold along a curve and neither can: both have to bend, and that is where the shell shapes come from.

cards.title: Concertina book of chequered rooms
cards.text: A black and white book stood open on its folds. Every spread is a room with a tiled floor, doorways and figures, so reading it is walking through it.

cards.title: Tunnel book of green hills
cards.text: Cut layers of hills hang between two concertina sides. Seen through the frame at the front, the flat sheets read as one deep valley.

cards.title: Paper theatre of a villa and garden
cards.text: A set of cut and coloured prints made to stand one behind another, so the garden steps back to the villa. The layers of the tunnel book, nearly three centuries ago.

cards.title: Tunnel book of a glass-roofed hall
cards.text: A cream paper bellows pulled open. Through the cut openings you look down a long hall under an arched glass roof, built up from printed layers.

cards.title: Book that opens into a round castle
cards.text: Opened until its covers meet, the book stands as a ring of walls with arched doors and battlements. Each gap between the pages is a chamber.

cards.title: Book of cut-out house fronts
cards.text: Every page is a house front with its windows cut through. Fanned open, the pages lean on one another like a street of roofs.

cards.title: Star book in red, black and grey
cards.text: Layered pages with frames cut out of them, opened round into a star. You look through one frame into the next, as you do in the castle.

cards.title: Concertina with three small boxes
cards.text: A folded cream card with a shallow box set into each panel, each holding a misty photograph. One box reads “beside a villa”: three rooms to look into.

cards.title: Grey concertina of open cells
cards.text: A printed strip folded so that its panels close into a row of square cells. It stands on the table like a terrace of small rooms.

cards.title: Notched boards slotted into a tower
cards.text: Brown boards with a notch in each edge, pushed into one another at right angles. There is no fold here at all: the slot does the work.

cards.title: Paper discs slotted at right angles
cards.text: Round sheets of tan paper with slits at the rim, each slid onto the next. The cluster stands on its plinth with only the slots holding it.

cards.title: Tower of orange and pink planes
cards.text: Flat pieces of bright card, slotted together at odd angles into a leaning spire. The same joint as the boards, used loosely.

cards.title: House of Cards
cards.text: Children build a tower of playing cards that only lean on one another. A slot is what a house of cards lacks: cut one and the cards would hold.
cards.by: Jean Michel Liotard, after François Boucher

cards.title: A slot is a joint with no glue
cards.text: Two flat pieces, each cut part of the way, lock at right angles. Each keeps the other from falling over, and they come apart again.

cards.title: Cardboard modules as tall as a person
cards.text: Two kits shown beside a figure for scale: “Module Rond” turns on a cut circle, “Module Fente” joins by slits. The same slots, large enough to stand behind.

cards.title: Towers of cardboard cubes with holes
cards.text: A man stands between two towers of brown card cubes and carries a ring of them on his shoulders. One small unit, repeated until it is taller than he is.

cards.title: Grey card cells locked into a block
cards.text: Two hands hold a cluster of six-sided tubes joined by short square ones, all cut from grey card. It looks like a unit that could go on in every direction.

cards.title: Diagram: prisms packed, then extruded
cards.text: A figure in steps: choose prisms that fill space, pull them apart, extrude their faces, then repeat the cell. The blue block it ends with looks like the card cluster.

cards.title: Reconfigurable prismatic materials
cards.text: Starts from prisms that fill space and extrudes their faces into thin-walled cells with hinges. The blocks that result can fold between several shapes.

cards.title: Paper strip looped into a figure eight
cards.text: A study model: one white strip with openings cut along it, bent into two loops. The tiny figures set beside it turn it into a building.

cards.title: Möbius strip made of paper
cards.text: A strip of green paper, 11 inches long, given a half twist and taped end to end. The simplest looping model there is.

cards.title: White model of a twisted ring
cards.text: A ring that turns over on itself, built up in thin layers and lit on a black table. The paper loop, given thickness.

cards.title: Looping ring in a hall, with its plan
cards.text: Above, a white band loops through a glazed hall with people walking under it. Below, its plan: a figure eight.

cards.title: Drawing of a looping ramp
cards.text: A ramp drawn in yellow that rises, crosses over itself and comes back round, with the circles and axes used to set it out.

cards.title: Dürer’s manual of measurement
cards.text: A page that plots a rising spiral from a circle cut into twelve parts: the plan below, the elevation above. The setting-out behind a looping ramp.

cards.title: Tilted ring of steps in a frame
cards.text: A dark rendering of a ring made of thin slats, tipped inside a frame marked 15 m wide and 9 m high. People are climbing it.

cards.title: Paper strips bent into walls
cards.text: Seen from above: white strips stood on edge on a brown base and pinned into S-curves. Rooms appear where the curves nearly touch.

cards.title: Wavy walls with figures between them
cards.text: The same idea drawn clean: curved walls laid out like a loose weave, with small black figures walking through the gaps.

cards.title: From Folds to Structures, a Review
cards.text: A review that starts from simple paper folding and follows it into structures: folded tessellations, and the ways engineers model them.

cards.title: Printed page of cut-and-fold exercises
cards.text: Page 21 of a book: diagrams lettered A to I show where to score, cut and fold a sheet, beside photographs of what results. Folding as a lesson.

cards.title: Single page book folding instruction
cards.text: Another instruction sheet, typed, with five figures: fold an 11 by 17 inch sheet into eight panels, cut one slit along the middle, and push it into a book.

cards.title: Models of Paper Folding (Origata tehon)
cards.text: A Japanese album of folded paper models, shown with its loose pieces laid out and labelled in ink. Folding written down as something to copy.

cards.title: Stencil with Pattern of Fans on Water
cards.text: A Japanese stencil of paper strengthened with silk: folding fans adrift on swirls of water. Folded paper as the picture, cut paper as the tool.

cards.title: Pleated animals from Li tre trattati
cards.text: An engraved plate from an Italian book of 1639: birds, dogs and a two-headed eagle built up from fine pleats, with folding patterns numbered at the edges.

cards.title: Folding fan, paper and wood
cards.text: A pleated paper leaf on wooden sticks, painted in gold on black. The pleats let it shut to a stick and open into a stiff half circle.
